newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil due lower after U.S. stocks data.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil due lower after U.S. stocks data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures are due to open weaker on Wednesday, dragged lower by overnight losses on U.S. markets following the release of bearish inventory data, brokers said.
June gas oil, which settled at $170 a tonne on Tuesday, is expected to begin trading about $2 lower while July Brent should come in 15-20 cents below its close of $18.90 a barrel, they said.
American Petroleum Insitute (API) figures released late on Tuesday showed a sharp 8.4 million-barrel build in crude stocks despite record gasoline production as refineries ran flat out.
"This set of figures is probably the most bearish I've seen for a long time," said a floor broker.

Brent, already reeling from a 62-cent slide on Tuesday sparked partly by anticipation of the API report but also by confirmation that the U.S. will support renewal of the U.N. oil-for-food deal with Iraq, will take another early hit.
But brokers said the impact of the U.S. stocks figures would be muted, unless confirmed by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)'s own regular weekly report due later on Wednesday.
"The API report is bearish but London will not be too aggressive," said a broker.
"There has to be a question mark over the refinery throughputs - it's impossible to have runs that high," he added.

Refinery runs rose 187,000 bpd to nearly 12.45 million bpd, putting operating capacity nationwide at 98.4 percent, or 99.9 percent in the states covered by Petroleum Administration for Defence Districts (PADDs) one to four.
Builds in stocks of middle distillates and more significantly gasoline, which usually sets the pace for oil prices at this time of year, would also keep product markets under pressure, brokers said.
